channel.title: Federal Farmer on The Anti-Federalist Library
channel.description: Recent content in Federal Farmer on The Anti-Federalist Library

item.title: Farmer I
item.description: Warns that the new Constitution consolidates too much power at the national level, threatening state sovereignty and individual freedoms.

item.title: Farmer II
item.description: Argues the proposed government would be too distant and removed from the people, weakening representation and accountability.

item.title: Farmer III
item.description: Claims that the Constitution’s powers over taxation and the military are too expansive, leading to potential tyranny.

item.title: Farmer IV
item.description: Critiques the proposed Senate, arguing that its members will be detached from the people and will become a permanent, elite ruling class.

item.title: Farmer V
item.description: Opposes the lack of a Bill of Rights, stressing that explicit protections are necessary to safeguard individual liberties.

item.title: Farmer VI
item.description: Questions the effectiveness of the Constitution’s checks and balances, arguing they are insufficient to prevent abuses of power.

item.title: Farmer VII
item.description: Concerns about the potential for a strong national government to override state governments and harm local interests.

item.title: Farmer VIII
item.description: Warns against the creation of a standing army under federal control, fearing it could be used to subjugate the states and people.

item.title: Farmer IX
item.description: Believes that the new Constitution will lead to a powerful executive branch that could threaten republican values and liberty.

item.title: Farmer X
item.description: Argues the system proposed by the Constitution will lead to a national government that undermines the rights and powers of the states.

item.title: Farmer XI
item.description: Expresses concern that the absence of a Bill of Rights in the new Constitution would leave citizens vulnerable to government overreach.

item.title: Farmer XII
item.description: Critiques the centralization of power in the federal government, claiming it will diminish the importance of local governments and lead to corruption.

item.title: Farmer XIII
item.description: Fears that the federal judiciary will undermine the authority of state courts, leading to an imbalance of power and loss of rights for citizens.

item.title: Farmer XIV
item.description: Warns that the Senate will become too powerful and disconnected from the people, effectively creating an aristocracy.

item.title: Farmer XV
item.description: Criticizes the proposed method for electing senators, arguing it concentrates power in the hands of a few, sidelining the people’s influence.

item.title: Farmer XVI
item.description: Argues that the powers given to the federal government are too broad, threatening the liberties of the states and individuals.

item.title: Farmer XVII
item.description: Warns that the lack of term limits and the extensive powers of the federal government will lead to corruption and a permanent political elite.

item.title: Farmer XVIII
item.description: Calls for a more balanced system that preserves state sovereignty and limits federal overreach, stressing the need for a Bill of Rights.
